scope: Theorem 4.1 (Refinement) of the manuscript “An Almost-Linear Approximation Scheme for Edit Distance” (preprints/An-Almost-Linear-Approximation-Scheme-for-Edit-Distance-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 121 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7ecda63faaa7d6a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Use the parameters and interval tree of Section 2 in the large-input branch. Let A be a power of two with 1 ≤ A ≤ Ainit, and let U be an integer table on every labeled tree node and every valid target state, with 0 ≤ U(I, q) ≤ N, c(I, q) ≤ U(I, q) ≤ Ac(I, q). Set a = max{1, A/F}. There is a randomized, finitely executable refinement table dS such that, for every state (I, q), dS(I, q) ≥ c(I, q)/a, E  (dS(I, q) − c(I, q))+  ≤ c(I, q)/ℓ. (4.1) The first inequality holds for every outcome of the refinement randomness; the expectation in the second is conditional on the fixed table U. At zero-cost states the returned value is zero for every outcome.
